claim: Alcatraz day tour costs $47.95 and night tour $59.65 per adult, with Alcatraz City Cruises the only NPS-authorized ferry provider, booking up to 90 days in advance.
quote: Day Tour Price: $47.95 for adults 18+ ... Night Tour Price: $59.65 ... Alcatraz City Cruises is the ONLY NPS-authorized ferry transportation provider to the Alcatraz Island ... purchased up to 90 days in advance

claim: Alcatraz tickets release 90 days out and in summer (June-August) routinely sell out 60-75 days ahead; night tours sell out fastest as ferries only run Tuesday-Saturday with lower capacity.
quote: During the peak summer months (June-August), they routinely sell out 60-75 days before the date ... Night ferries only run Tuesday through Saturday and capacity is much lower, so book even further in advance.

claim: As of January 1, 2026 the cable car single-ride fare is $9.00 for adults, $5.00 for youth 5-18, and $3.50 for seniors 65+ with valid ID.
quote: the base single-ride fare for the San Francisco cable car is $9.00 for adults (ages 19-64). Children aged 5-18 pay $5.00 ... Seniors (65+) ... pay $3.50

claim: SFMTA approved an $18 daily 'Cable Car Plus' pass (unlimited Muni for one adult plus up to two children) taking effect January 4, 2027, set to become the main option after the cheaper one-way fare is eliminated in 2028.
quote: $18 'Cable Car Plus' pass - Provides unlimited travel on all Muni services for one day for one adult and up to two children ... takes effect on January 4, 2027

claim: Coit Tower elevator entry is $11 for non-resident adults ($8 residents), with first-floor murals free during open hours, generally 10am-6pm April-October and 10am-5pm November-March.
quote: Elevator entrance prices: adults pay $8 for San Francisco residents and $11 for non-residents ... First-floor murals are free to view during open hours ... usually open daily from 10 am to 6 pm from April through October

claim: Fisherman's Wharf is reachable by classic cable car from downtown but is widely cautioned as the least appealing neighborhood to stay in, valued mainly for quick ferry access.
quote: warned not to get stuck in the tourist trap of Fisherman's Wharf, as staying there is the least appealing neighborhood, though it's great for quick access to ferries

claim: Battery Spencer in the Marin Headlands offers the premier free Golden Gate Bridge viewpoint via a 750-foot walk from a small free lot; walking the bridge itself is about 1.7 miles one way and takes 30-45 minutes.
quote: Battery Spencer offers one of the most breathtaking vantage points ... just a quick 750-foot walk from the parking lot ... The walk across the Golden Gate Bridge spans approximately 1.7 miles one way and typically takes about 30 to 45 minutes

claim: A local guide recommends the free Cable Car Museum and treats Lombard Street pragmatically as a quick photo stop on the Powell-Hyde line rather than a destination requiring a long visit.
quote: Cable Car Museum: 'Entry is free' ... you can see it from the cable car and 'walk down Lombard and take photos,' but also suggests alternatives if you'd prefer not to 'walk back up Lombard.'
